author: Sanketh Ramkrishnamurthy
content:
Most people think job applications are just numbers. Apply more. Get more chances.

But hiring doesn’t really work that way.

One thing many freshers and even experienced professionals don’t fully understand is how recruitment systems actually remember candidates.

When you apply for a role, your profile goes into an ATS an Applicant Tracking System. Platforms like JazzHR, Workday, Greenhouse, iCIMS and others don’t just store your resume. They store your application history too.

Every role you applied for. Every rejection. Every movement is connected to your profile.

𝐍𝐨𝐰 𝐡𝐞𝐫𝐞’𝐬 𝐰𝐡𝐞𝐫𝐞 𝐦𝐚𝐧𝐲 𝐜𝐚𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐝𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐬 𝐮𝐧𝐤𝐧𝐨𝐰𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐥𝐲 𝐡𝐮𝐫𝐭 𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐢𝐫 𝐨𝐰𝐧 𝐜𝐡𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞𝐬.

A Python developer applies for a Java backend role. Rejected.
Then applies for DevOps. Rejected again.
Then QA testing.
Then Product Support.

Months later, the company opens a Python role, the exact role the candidate is actually good at.

The recruiter opens the profile and immediately sees multiple past rejections across completely unrelated roles.

Before even reading the resume, one thought quietly forms:, “Is this person applying with clarity… or just applying everywhere?”

That changes perception faster than people realise.

Some apply to everything. Some apply to the right thing. And the difference shows not just in the resume, but in the way the application is put together.

The ATS tracks your applications. Recruiters track your intent.

When someone applies to ten different roles across teams, functions, experience levels, and locations within the same company, it often signals confusion rather than ambition.

And confusion is difficult to ignore.

One focused application tells me the candidate understands:
• the role
• the expectation
• their own strengths

𝐓𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐢𝐬 𝐰𝐡𝐲 𝐈 𝐚𝐥𝐰𝐚𝐲𝐬 𝐭𝐞𝐥𝐥 𝐬𝐭𝐮𝐝𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐬 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐟𝐞𝐬𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐚𝐥𝐬:

Read the complete JD carefully. Not just the title.

Understand the skills, responsibilities, expectations, and experience level.

Then honestly ask yourself, Can I map at least 70% of this role to what I genuinely know or can do?

If yes, apply with confidence.

If not, prepare first. Learn first. Wait for the right fit.

Also check:
Have you already applied to this company before?
For what kind of roles?
Does that history strengthen your profile or dilute it?

Strategy builds careers. Impulse delays them.

So before clicking “Apply,” pause for a moment and ask yourself:

“Do I genuinely belong in this role?”
“Would I be proud to grow here?”

If the answer is yes, apply with clarity and purpose. Make your profile speak well about you before you even enter the room. And if the answer is no, keep preparing.

The right opportunity is always worth waiting for.

Be selective enough that the system remembers you for the right reasons.
